| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

Addons have always been excluded from the terms, but this options can now be used to keep the addons in the terms discount calculation. Was added as part of the VAT migration project, but this option applies regardless of using VAT or not. |
| `allowgenericprodrebfl` | Allow Generic Prod Rebate | Logical | yes/no | Added with JIRA SXWEB-38291/SXWEB-39527. This field sets this vendor to participate on the Generic Rebates logic for Vendor on Sale rebates, when checked. It is located in APSV – Ordering – Rebates section with the label “Use Generic Rebates”. When a product is entered on the OE line, the vendor is looked up – in ICSW, ICSC, or from OEEL depending on the product being a stock, catalog, or non-stock product – to determine if that vendor is a generic product rebate vendor based on the APSV allow generic rebates flag. If that vendor allows generic rebates, the PDSR rebate logic will ignore the assigned vendor, except to limit the choices to vendors who use generic rebates. As soon as a record is found, ignoring the vendor, that rebate will be used and then the logic will continue to use all other criteria for finding the best rebate to use, e.g., it will still use the Customer Rebate Types listed for the customer in ARSC/ARSS and any other criteria such as customer/shipto/warehouse. So it is just ignoring the vendor when searching for the rebate to use but does not ignore any other criteria. Usage of this logic requires AOData PD - PDGenericVendProdRebateFl to be checked. This can be found in AO – Products – Rebates – Rebates Options section with the label “Allow Generic Product Rebates”. Content: |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

### Table ARET — AR Transactions

- Indexes: `k-cod`, `k-crjrnl`, `k-duedt`, `k-inq`, `k-invdt`, `k-invno`, `k-jrnl` (Primary), `k-rowpointer` (Unique), `k-transdttmz`, `k-udnet`

| Column | Label | Type | Format | Help / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `addonamt` | Addon | Decimal[4] | zzzzzzz9.99- | This array field has 2 occurances: Addon 1 Addon 2 These addons will default in from the ARSCO record. The addonamt is also updated from order entry during invoice processing. See addonamt field in oeeh for a further description. Content: |
| `amount` | Amount | Decimal | zzzzzzzz9.99- | This is the dollar amount for this transaction. This is enterable by the user in ARET. This is also updated during invoice processing. The total invoice amount on the order will become the amount on the ARET record. |
| `appinvdt` | Applied Inv Dt | Date | 99/99/99 | This field is updated on schedule pay (type 11), credit memo (type 6), and debit memo (type 8) records in the following mannor: Type 11 - schedule pay: This is the date that a credit memo or debit memo is applied to this schedule pay. The date comes in from the invoice date entered in aret for the credit memo or debit memo. Or, the invoice date of the RM applied through invoice processing. Type 06,08 - credit memo/debit memo: This is the date of the invoice this has been applied to. Misc credit or unapplied cash amounts applied in arece do NOT update this field. |
| `appinvdttz` | Time Zone Off Set | Datetime-tz | 99/99/9999 HH:MM:SS.SSS+HH:MM |  |
| `appinvno` | Applied Inv # | Integer | zzzzzzz9 | This field is updated on the following records: 11- schedule pay 06 - credit memo 08 - debit memo On the type 11, this is the invoice number of the credit memo, misc credit, or debit memo. On the type 06 and 08 this is the invoice number this transaction was applied to. |
| `appinvsuf` | Applied Inv Suffix | Integer | 99 | The applied invoice suffix. The suffix will be 00 - 98 if the invoice was created through invoice processing. The suffix will be -99 for invoices created in ARET. |
| `apptranscd` | Tran Type | Integer | 99 | This is the code of the transaction that was applied to this particular invoice. example: 05 - misc credit 06 - credit memo 08 - debit memo On the credit memo, misc credit or debit memo invoice, the apptranscd would be the transaction code of the invoice it was applied against. example: 00 - invoice 01 - service charge 04 - cod |
| `arexrate` | A/R Exchange Rate | Decimal | zzzzz9.9999999 |  |
| `checkno` | Check # | Decimal | zzzzzzz9 | The check number applied to this invoice/schedule pay. This field can be updated the following ways: The check is posted through ARECE. The check number is stored on the invoice (type 0) and the scheduled pay (type 11) record. The invoice record stores the most recently applied check number. The check is received through Order Entry Received On Account. The check number is stored on the Unappplied Cash (type 3) record. The check is posted through Order Entry downpayment. The check number is stored on the manual payment record (type 7). Miscellaneous credits (type 5) applied in arece with a cash posting transaction, the check number will be stored on the misc credit record. |
| `checknopaid` | Check# | Decimal | zzzzzzz9 | This field is updated on type 3 (unapplied cash) records. The field is updated with the check number being applied in arece when the unapplied cash is being applied. Only updated when the unapplied cash is inactivated. This field is not enterable by the user. |
| `codcollamt` | COD Collected | Decimal | zzzzzzzz9.99 | The purpose of this field is to collect an additional amount from the customer to go towards a past due amount. The amount will then display in arece when paying the cod. The amount does NOT display in arit. Amount is calculated in pmep, if the customer has an arsa record. Will also be calculated if invoice is cod, and additional amount entered in oees, or oeir. Amount is updated from the oeeh.codcollamt field. updated in oeepia.p and p-oeepip.i. Read in arececod.p and p-arra.i. |
| `cono` | Company # | Integer | >>>9 | Identifies the Company under which the record was created. |
| `crjrnlno` | Cash Rec Applied Jrnl # | Integer | >>>>>>>9 | This is the arece journal number. This field is updated when type 5 (misc credit) and type 3(unapplied cash) transactions are applied in arece. Program that updates this field is areceu1.p Field is displayed in arit for inactive type 3 and 5 transactions. Not enterable by user. |
| `crsetno` |  | Integer | >>9 | This is the set number of the arece posting journal. Only updates type 5 (misc credit) and type 3 (unapplied cash) transactions. This set number is not displayed in arit. Updated in areceu1.p and displays on ar journal print. Not enterable by the user. |
| `custno` | Customer # | Decimal | zzzzzzzzzzz9 | The customer number for this invoice. This field is entered in arece, aret and oeet. |
| `discamt` | Discount | Decimal | zzzzzzz9.99- | The amount of discount actually taken, versus the original discount amount calculated for this invoice. This field is updated when the schedule pay is paid. Initially defaults in as zero. updated on the type 00, 11, 07, and 05 records. |
| `discdt` |  | Date | 99/99/99 | This is the date the invoice must be paid otherwise the order discount is considered lost. This date is calculated from the disount days on the terms record set up in sastt. Each customer will have a terms type set up on the arsc required screen. This date can be overrode in aret, aremo and aremp. |
| `discdttz` | Time Zone Off Set | Datetime-tz | 99/99/9999 HH:MM:SS.SSS+HH:MM |  |
| `disputefl` |  | Logical | yes/no | This field has a value of y/n. This field designates a transaction as disputed. Transactions that are disputed are not aged or service charged. This field is enterable by the user in aret and aremo. Transactions that are disputed display a 'h' next to the invoice date of the schedule pay in arit and a 'd' next to the seq number of the schedule pay in arece. There is a dispute field on the f6 detail record in aret. This will display yes on the schedule pay records. It will only display yes on the invoice record if the invoice was flagged as disputed when entered in aret. If the invoice was not entered as disputed, but was flagged as disputed in aremo, the invoice detail will show 'no' in the dispute field. However, the PY will show yes. This is because the invoice was not disputed at time of entry, and in aremo the schedule pay is being disputed. 2-27-94 fef |
| `divno` | Division # | Integer | >>>9 | Division # |
| `duedt` |  | Date | 99/99/99 | The date this invoice is due for payment. The due date is calculated based on the terms type for this customer. The due date can be overridden. |
| `duedttz` | Time Zone Off Set | Datetime-tz | 99/99/9999 HH:MM:SS.SSS+HH:MM |  |
| `exchgrate` | Exchange Rate | Decimal[2] | zzzzz9.9999999 | Exchange rate |
| `glacctno` | Acct# | Integer | zzzzzzzz9 | GL account Number |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

| `mancommcalcty` | Calculate Sales Rep Commission From | Character | x(2) | A distributor may elect to pay a portion of the Manufacturer Commisison paid to the distributor with the sales reps on the Manufacturer Rep Orders. During SMRC when the commission is determined for the sales reps of the orders, this option will determine on the Man rep Orders how the rate is applied. Against the Sales Amount of the lines (netamt) or the Commission Amount paid to the distributor from the vendor. the default is Blank (Earned Commission Amount) versus the Sales Amount Content: |
| `mancustprintty` | Print Invoice For | Character | x(2) | In most cases the Manufacturer Rep Order does not need to print during invoice processing. The order is used in CSD to determine commission payment from the vendor and the vendor already has an order in their system for the customer. the goods are shipped to the customer from the vendor and the vendor bills the customer. This option allows the Manufacturer Orders to print differently from the Floor Plan print option on the OEEPI report. It is setup per vendor since each vendor may require copies of the orders or the distributor may want hard copies of the orders Content: |
| `mansalesfl` | Manufacturer Vendor | Logical | yes/no | This is a customer that is really a vendor. The customer will be used on Manufacturer Rep Orders orders as the floor plan customer - who is paying the invoice. - Address will be the vendor's address - billing terms (terms type) will be for the vendor payment The Manufacturer Rep Orders ARET Invoice Amouts for ARECE are determined off the Commission paid from the vendor to the Distributor (whse). Commission Rates paid to the distributor are setup in OESM |
| `manusesalesrepfl` | Use Sales Rep In/Out For Commission Paid | Logical | yes/no | This option controls where the Inside/Outside sales reps on the Manufacturer Orders default from for this vendor. Use the Manufacturer Vendor Customer sales reps or use the Ordering Customer/Ship to sales reps on the Manufacturer Rep Order as defaults It is a way to override sales reps since the orders are not typical sales orders. Sales reps can manually be changed per order as well |

| `orderreppct1` | Order Rep 1 Percent | Decimal | zz9.99 | This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content: |

Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

| `orderreppct1` | Order Rep 1 Percent | Decimal | zz9.99 | This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content: |

Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content: |

| `exceptmsg` | Exception Message | Character | x(60) | If an exception is found during cartonization, then the message is stored on the exception carton. The Carton ID is the Order#: "o1234-00 - Exception" and the statusty of the crton record (icecnhdr.statusty) is 'E'. Exceptions can be deleted once corrected via the ICECN 'Delete Packages' function. Repack the item manually, or delete the package if one is created for the order and re-run auto cartonization. |
| `height` | Item Height | Decimal | zzzzz9.99999 | Height of the item being packaged. If the unit on the order line is linked to a Product specific ICSEU record and that record is setup to calculate/store dimensions (icseu.cncalcpkgsizefl) to be able to pack that container inside another container. So it is the Height of the Unit (Container) - Case - Box Content: |

How much of the items will fit Cubic Feet Dimension. Height, Width, Length of the carton are measured in Inches, Feet, Yards, Centimeters or Milimeters. Those dimensions are all convered to inches and multiplied together and divided by 1728 to get the cubic feet dimension to be used to see what can fit into the carton dimensionally Content: |

### Table ICECNHDR — Cartonization Package Header

| `actweight` | Actual Weight (Billable) | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | This is the Actual Weight for the package which is entered in ICECN during the Shipping process of the Packages. There are three weights on the package Actual Dimensional Package |
| `cartonid` | Carton ID | Character | x(30) | Carton ID of the Package being Shipped. See the different 'Format' options from AO and ICSD. There can be up to four different sections to a Carton ID, or just one. The company can determine what to use and in what position. Sections can be: Whse Package Type Carton Number Additional Lettering If the order/detail has an exception during Cartonization, then Carton ID is the Order#: "o1234-00 - Exception" |
| `cartonno` | Carton Number | Integer | zzzzzzzz9 | The carton number is a system generated number from a database sequence trigger. Incremental. This is the only section of the Carton ID that is required. We store the carton number on the package. |
| `cono` | Company | Integer | zzz9 | Company Numer - SASC Content: |
| `dimdivsor` | Dimensional Weight Divisor | Integer | zz9 | Transportation Standard Carrier - Extended Screen Dimensional Weight Divisor. Used with a carrier to determine the minimum weight per box to use for lighter shipments. It will use the Dimensional Weight if it is higher than the actual weight of a box for the billable weight of the package. Cartons Dimensional Cubic Feet / Dimensional Divisor Content: |
| `dimweight` | Dimensional Weight | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | Cartons Dimensional Cubic Feet / Dimensional Divisor Compared to the Actual Weight of the Package. It will default in the Dimensional Weight if the Dimensional Weight is more. Prevents lighter items shipping with fright changes that are too low |
| `freefreightfl` | Free Freight | Logical | yes/no | The package can be flagged as a 'Free' shipping package. A promotional shipment or special deal. Loaded as 'free' manaully in ICECN when shipping the Cartons - where Freight and Actual Weight is entered. |

| `instructions` | Package Instructions | Character | x(60) | These are the instructions pulled from the Carton Setup - ICSCN for the specific package being used. Stored on the record for display of the carton instructions or use in Package Labels if the customer want's them to display. Content: |
| `operinit` | Operator | Character | x(4) |  |
| `pkgcubesize` | Package Cube Size | Decimal | zzzzzzzz9.99999 | The dimensional Cube Size of the carton - not the items in the carton, but the carton itself. This is used when comparing the Items to put in the carton. How much of the items will fit Cubic Feet Dimension. Height, Width, Length of the carton are measured in Inches, Feet, Yards, Centimeters or Milimeters. Those dimensions are all convered to inches and multiplied together and divided by 1728 to get the cubic feet dimension to be used to see what can fit into the carton dimensionally |
| `pkggroupty` | Package Group | Character | x(8) | When a package is a special package and links to specific items, then the Package Group Type can be used to group specific items together in a specific package. Dry Ice container Drum for liquid Content: |

| `pkgno` | Package Number | Integer | zz9 | This links the Package to an OEEHP record package number. OEEHP records are created from the Shipping interface, but are numeric numbers. Cartonization packages are based on Carton ID's. Initially, the only way to link an external shipped package to a Cartonization Package is manaully entering the Package Number from the Shipping Interface to the Package in ICECN during the Shipping of the Carton - when entering the Weight and Freigh charges. It can be an informaitonal field that is manually entered during the shipping process in ICECN and not be linked to OEEHP records at all. |
| `pkgtype` | Package Type | Character | x(8) | This is a way to link specific types of packages to specific types of items. There is a package type stored on the ICSP/ICSC records. Content: |
| `pkgweight` | Package Weight | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | This is the combined weight of all the items in the package. This is the weigh totalled from the ICSP Weight (Stocking) converted to the unit conversion on the line of the order and then multipled by the quantity in the box for the item. A system generated weight. This will default in as the weight during shipping of the package, but the opertor will enter in the Actual Weight of the package to be compared to the Dimensional Weight. The system weight is used during cartonization to find packages and compare to package min/max weight settings. |
| `rowpointer` | Row Pointer | Character | x(36) | System generated GUID Unique identifier of the record Loads in the Detail Carton record - icecndtl.icecnhdrrowpointer to show what cartons all the items are connected to |
| `shippingid` | Shipment ID | Character | x(30) | The operator can select to manually enter a Shipping ID to be attached to the Cartons via ICECN - when running Auto Cartonization. The operator can enter in an ASN Number, a Truck Number. The ID is a way to link all the orders in the Cartonization process together. An easy way in ICECN to see all the cartons for a Shipment - Advance Search. If a Shipping ID is chosen to be created automatically (from ICECN or the Picking runs - OEEPP/WTEP), it will be in the following format: YYYYMMDD-HH:MM:SS-zz9 |

Normally generated from the third party shipping interface - UPS, FedEx to track the packages. ICECN allows for manual entry of the tracking ID. ### Table ICET — IC Transaction Entry

- Source page: `icettbl.htm`
- Indexes: `k-jrnl`, `k-ordno`, `k-postdt` (Primary), `k-prod`, `k-rowpointer` (Unique), `k-transdttmz`, `k-usgwhse`

| Column | Label | Type | Format | Help / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `apinvno` | Vendor Invoice | Character | x(15) |  |
| `cono` | Company # | Integer | >>>9 | Identifies the Company under which the record was created. |
| `cost` | Cost | Decimal | >>>>>>>.99999 | This is the cost as is occurs on this individual record. It corresponds to the G/L entry for this specific record. As such, it will include add-ons if capitalizing them (incoming through PO) or if included in SM/GL cost (outgoing). The cost is always in domestic currency, is always in stocking units, and always represents a per unit cost, to be matched with the units on the record. If the item is a special price/cost item (see ICSP), the cost on the ICET record will represent the cost per special price/cost unit, not per stocking unit. This is referred to as the 'raw' cost. |
| `custno` | Customer # | Character | x(12) | Customer number, as in Trend Standard. Present only on records that relieve inventory through Order Entry or on returned goods through Order Entry. It is validated against ARSC. |
| `divno` | Division # | Integer | >>>9 | The division number of the warehouse affected by the transaction. In most situations, this division will be the same as the ICSD division. You can, however, choose to have the division number loaded from the customer record. In this case ICET records that are associated with customer transactions will be loaded with the division number from the customer record. All other cases and all other settings will produce a division number matching that of ICSD. This is the recommended use of the the field. |
| `enterdt` | Entered | Date | 99/99/99 | The creation date of the record. This is set to be equal to the variable 'g-today'. This global variable always equals the current system date except when scheduled reports go past midnight, in which case it represents the date when the report should have run. |
| `enterdttz` | Time Zone Off Set | Datetime-tz | 99/99/9999 HH:MM:SS.SSS+HH:MM |  |
| `exchgrate` | IC Exchange Rate | Decimal | zzzzz9.9999999 | Used With Foreign Currency Accounts |
| `icspcrowpointer` | ICSPC Row Pointer | Character | x(36) |  |
| `icspecrecno` | Spec Rec Link | Decimal | >>>>>>9 | Special Price/Cost Record Number for Link to Transactions |
| `icswcost` | ICSW Cost | Decimal | >>>>>>9.99999- | This represents the SM/GL as it existed BEFORE the application of the current posting function (the one creating this record). If appropriate, this includes the average add-on figure. This field is very important as it represents the only way of figuring a cost for the valuation of inventory for an 'as of' trial balance. The ICRT report uses this figure from the first record posted AFTER the cutoff date to calculate total value. It is critical that every ICET record create record this figure prior to any recalculations. If the product is a special price/cost item (see ICSP) then this cost is in the special price/cost unit, not the stocking unit. This is called the 'raw' cost. |
| `jrnlno` | Jrnl # | Integer | >>>>>>>9 | journal # |
| `lineno` | Line# | Integer | >>9 | Line Number is the line number from the supporting document for this transaction. The use will vary depending on the document type. It is a valid field only for those transactions created from a document (OE,PO, etc.) |
| `mergedfl` | Merged | Logical | yes/no | The Merged flag is used to control updates to ICSWU from ICAM. This flag is set to 'no' by all procedures that create ICET and is set to 'yes' by the ICAM process itself. |
| `module` | Module | Character | x(2) | This represents the Trend module that created the ICET transaction. IT follows the Trend 'ouproc' name, not 'currproc'. It is important that 'ourproc' is used to ensure that reports and inquiries can find the proper record regardless of source. If the option is set to yes, then the outbound BOD will send the Header and Detail information that is attached to the order. | `cnctnlettercd` | Last Lettering Code Used in Carton ID | Character | x(2) | Both cnusecartonidfl and cnctnletterfl have to be turned on to use this setting When using the letter code in the Carton ID, the system starts the Letter Coce as 'AA' and will increment with each carton it is used in. ie - AA, AB, AC, AD . . . . to ZZ, then starts over. It is an updatable field, but will show in ICSD, the last Letter Code used by the system. |

If all four sections in use, then can be 1-4, three sections 1-3, two sections 1-2, or just the number - 1. Content: |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

Content: |

### Table ICSGK — Catalog Group Keys - This table serves a dual purpose. The first purpose is to create an environment in which a store can easily add products to a branch of a tree or create a branch without having to know the specific nodeid for that node on the tree. This will be accomplished by using a tag that is specific to each store or by using a product which has already been placed on the tree as a reference product. The second purpose is to allow us to report on and manage the store specific tree structure.

| `corecharge` | Core Charge | Decimal | zzzzz9.99 | The standard core charge, if any, for this product. The core charge will be charged to the customer on any sale. It can be overridden from the extented screen (F7) in Order Entry. During a return, the customer can be credited with the product charge (price), the core charge, or both. Core charges are used as a deposit-like system in two situations: 1) When buying a rebuilt item (electric motors for example) where the old, defective item will be rebuilt and resold. 2) When buying something that requires a returnable container, such as gases in a tank. The customer is charge for both the item and the core. When the old item or the container is returned, the customer gets a core credit. |

| `cubes` | Cube | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99999 | The size, in cubes, represented by a single stocking unit of this particular item. This field is generally for user information, printing on pick tickets and a few reports. There are two situations, however, where the value of this field becomes important: 1) Order Targets by Cube. Cube can be used as a target method in ICSL. If so, the cube value * the quantity ordered is used for target and minimum buy information. Note also that if target is cube, the total volume in APSP will be by cube and review cycles will be calculated using total cubes and target cubes. 2) If using warehouse manager and calculating bin capacity by cube, this field is used to determine the total quantity of product that can fit in a bin and the space available in any bin containing this product. For this purpose it is important that cube is as accurate as possible. |

It is set to 'no' by the deletion of the last ICSEU record for this product. The flag is used in the 'p-unit.i' object to speed the validation of entered units. |
| `unitsell` | Selling Units | Character | x(4) | The selling unit is used as a default for all order entry processes. If entered, it is validated against ICSEU and SASTT entries. If left blank, all selling processes will default to the stocking unit. Note that this is used only as a default, not a mandatory selling unit. |
| `unitstock` | Stocking Units | Character | x(4) | The stocking unit is required for every product. It is not validated against any unit setups and is always assumed to represent a single unit in all quantity fields for the product. It is normally 'each'. It is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED that the stocking unit be the smallest possible selling unit to avoid fractional quantities. The stocking unit is also used as an automatic default for all other units for the product. Any unit (other than stocking) that is left blank will be considered equal to the stocking unit. The stocking unit is the basis for all quantity transactions in Trend. As such, it is very important to not change the value of this field in mid-stream. Careful consideration must be given to the effect on: 1) Quantities and Balances in ICSW 2) Pricing in ICSW, PDS* 3) Outstanding orders, transfers, purchase orders 4) GL Balances 5) History on file |

This field is used only if using the special pricing/costing unit conversion (see speccostty). Note that this field cannot be negative, but will often be less than one. Note also the direction of conversion - number of special units in a stocking unit. This date is maintained automatically by all receiving processes. This works in conjunction with the last stock out date and the number of days stock out to make extended stock out decisions for ICAM. | `avgcost` | Average | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99999 | Average Cost. This field is maintained by the system and should not be changed by the user. It is protected by the see cost flag in SASOO. This field is an integral part of IC balancing. The average cost represents the average cost of the items in stock. It is updated by all process affecting inventory quantities. This field is stored either in stocking units or in 'raw' cost - special price/cost units. Average cost is updated during receiving by taking the old cost times the old qty, adding the received quantity times the new cost, and dividing the sum by the new total quantity: $10 * 50 = 500 $15 * 10 = 150 == === 60 650 $650 / 60 = 10.833 each A similar process is done if items are removed from stock at any cost other than average. IC Balancing documents explain the entire process. |

It is calculated by ICAM and includes safety stock. The calculation is usage during the ordering period (determined by lead time) plus safety stock. For example: 30 used per month 10 days lead time 50% safety stock Used during lead time = 10 (one per day for ten days lead time) Safety Stock = 5 (50% of usage during lead time or 10) Order Point = 15 |

| `fulfillmentstgcd` | Fulfillment Stage | Character | x(2) | This will track the stage of the Fulfillment Order. From the time it is initially entered to the point of being ready to invoice through Consolidated Invoicing. If the system it set to not do fulfillment billing through consolidated invoicing, then the only stages that are used in the sustem are Open, eCommerce and Submitted. OERC will look at Tied Order associated with Fulfillment orders in stage Submitted, Released and Consolidated. Content: |
| `fulfillmenttiedfl` | Tied Fulfillment Order | Logical | yes/no | Tied Fulfillment Order are created from the original Fulfillment Order once the operator selects the Warehouses or Ties to be used to fill the line items and Submit is choosen from OEET, OEIF, or SXAPI Full Order Maint (based on OESF SXAPI Auto Submit option setting). If a Stock Order is tied to a Fulfillment Order (Created from it), then the tied flag is set. The only tie to the fulfillment order is through the OEELO record that is attached to the original fulfillment order - showing what Tied Fulfillment Orders are associated with the fulfillment order. Once the Tied Order is created, the Tied Order shows the original fulfillment order it came from by looking at the fulfillment orderno/oordersuf fields. Content: |
| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

Against the Sales Amount of the lines (netamt) or the Commission Amount paid to the distributor from the vendor. The value is pulled in from the ARSC Manufacturer Vendor customer setting, but loaded on the order for use in SMRC and commission to the sales reps Content: |
| `manexppaydt` | Expected Commission Payment | Date | 99/99/99 | When is the Vendor expected to make payment of the commission for this order. Compared against the actual Paid date of the order. Initially calculated off the Request Ship Date and the Manufacturer Customer terms setting (Req Ship Date + Due Date) Once the Actual Manufacturer Shipment Date (oeeh.manactshipdt) is entered by the operator, then the date is recalcuated based on the Terms of the Manufacture Sales Customer (Terms Due Date + Expected Ship Date) Informational Only. In place for Birst Reporting Content: |
| `mansalesorderty` | Manufacturer Order Type | Character | x(2) | New type of order in OE - Manufacture Rep Order. Will be an order that strictly tracks Sales and Commission payment from the Manufacturer Vendor. This are orders that mirror the orders in the vendors system. No inventory shipped to the customer since the vendor is billing the customer and shipping the goods to the customer The vendor is giving the distributor a commission for sending them the sale A total sales order only tracks a total commissopn amount and a total sales amount. The distributor only knows those totals and ntohgin about the actual orders in the vendor's system - no items. A commission check was sent with only those totals and the order did not exist in CSD with specifics of the order Content: |

| `nocatwght` | # Cat Wt | Integer | >>9 | The number of line items for which catch weight quantities need to be entered. This field is automatically updated as line items are maintained. An order can not be invoiced until the charge quantity has been entered on all lines that require entry of a charge quantity. ### Table OEEHBR — Order Entry Blanket Release Header

| `orderreppct5` | Order Rep 5 Percent | Decimal | zz9.99 | This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content: |

This field starts out as 0 (since the order has not yet been picked). It remains 0 when the pick ticket is printed. Any time the quantity/unit on the line is maintained after picking, the prevqtyshp is loaded with the old stock quantity that was shipped. The prevqtyshp will not be overridden again until after the pick ticket is reprinted. This field controls the "Print Changes Only" option in picking. Content: |

### Table OEELB — OE Batch Line Items

| `arpprodline` | ARP Line | Character | x(6) | The product line or warehouse this product is sourced from. This field is only loaded for non-stock products, special order items, and drop ship lines. For a non-stock product, this field is enterable on the non-stock screen. If the ARP whse on the non-stock screen is entered, the arpprodline will contain the whse and the arpvendno will be 0. If the ARP whse is not entered on the non-stock screen, the arpprodline will contain the product line entered on the non-stock screen. For a stocked product, this field defaults from either the ARP whse (if the ARP is a whse) or the ARP product line set in ICSW. This field is used for special and non-stock lines that need to be picked up on a RRAR. Content: |
| `arpvendno` | ARP Vendor # | Decimal | >>>>>>>>>>>9 | The ARP vendor number is used to indicate who the line is sourced from (if sourced from a vendor). It is only loaded on a non-stock product, special order line, or drop ship line. On a non-stock, it is loaded with the vendor entered on the non-stock screen. For a stocked special or DO line, it is loaded with the ARP vendor from ICSW. If the line is a DO line or tied line, the vendor is overrideable from the F6 function key on the extended screen. If no vendor exists in ICSW, this field will contain a 0. Content: |
| `batchnm` | Batch | Character | x(8) | The batch name is the key to this record with the company and sequence number. These fields tie one batch together. Content: |
| `botype` | B/O | Character | x | (Y)es, (N)o, (P)ickup |
| `bplineno` | BP Line # | Integer | zzz9 |  |
| `cataddfl` | Added From Catalog | Logical | yes/no | Indicates if an order as needed product was added from the catalog when this line was added. If the product was not set up when the line was added but was defined in the catalog file, the operator has the option to create an ICSP/ICSW record automatically. If the new records are created, this flag is set to yes. If the catalog product is pulled into the order as a non-stock product, this flag remains no. OERE reports all products added from the catalog file as lines are added. Content: |
| `chrgqty` | Charge Qty | Decimal | >>>>>>9.99- | The charge quantity for a catch weight product. This field is enterable on the extended screen in OEES. It is used to reprice/cost the line items based on the weight of the line. (NOTE: we now longer allow entry of a catch weight product in ICSP as of V3.0. Keep all code intact in case we reestablish this functionality.) Content: |
| `commentfl` | Comment | Logical | yes/no |  |
| `commtype` | Commission | Character | x(4) | Describes whether the commission amount is a % or a $. Content: |
| `cono` | Company # | Integer | >>>9 | Identifies the Company under which the record was created. |
| `corecharge` | Core Charge | Decimal | zzzzz9.99 | The core charge for the product. This charge defaults to the line item from ICSP. It is expressed in the selling unit of measure. |
| `corechgty` | Core Charge | Character | x | (Y)es, (N)o, or (R)eturn |
| `costoverfl` | Cost Over | Logical | yes/no | The cost override flag indicates if the cost has been manually entered. Content: |
| `crreasonty` | Credit Memo Reason | Character | x(2) | The credit reason type. If this field is entered on the banner on a CR or RM order, it will default to the line item. It can be overridden on a return line when F17 is pressed to return a line. Content: |
| `datccost` | DATC | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99999 | The "destination area transportation charge" for this line item represented in the selling unit. The field was originally established to be a datc cost. It has since be expanded (V4.5) to be a line addon charge. The label of the cost is user defined. If it is defined in ICAO, this charge can be entered (and will default from ICSW). This field is used to pass an additional charge to the customer based on the product sold and how it is sold (IE: if the product was rushed to the customer). Content: |
| `discamt` | Discount | Decimal | >>>>>>9.99999 | The discount amount of the line item. This field is represented in the selling unit of measure (if the product is a specially costed product, this field is represented in the special costing unit). The discount amount can be calculated from the PDSC setup (and is thus a % discount). It can also be manually overridden and set to a $ discount. |
| `disctype` | Discount Type | Logical | $/% | $ or % |
| `enterdt` | Entered | Date | 99/99/99 | The date the order was added. When a back order is created, the enter date is reset to the date the back order is created. |

| `jitpickfl` | JIT Picked | Logical | yes/no | This flag indicates that a "just in time" line item has been picked. JIT orders are established by an orderdisp of "j". Only lines that should be picked based on the promise date of the line item will be picked. When these lines are picked, the jitpickfl will be set to yes. Once the line is set to yes, it qualifies for shipping and invoicing. The lines not picked will move to a new release when the lines that have been picked are invoiced. Content: |
| `jobno` | Job # | Character | x(8) | The job number on the line item. This number defaults from the job number attached to the ARSS record. If a job number exists on the PDSC record that is used for pricing, it will override the ARSS job number. This field prints on the PO and WT RRAR reports. |

If the product is not taxable, it defaults from the ICSW non tax reason. Otherwise it is set to the header non tax reason. Content: |

It is overrideable on the extended screen and the non-stock screen. G/L posting can be done by product category. Content: |

If the product is not specially costed, this field is represented in the selling unit on the line item. | `altwhse` | Alt Whse | Character | x(4) | The alternate warehouse if an alternate warehouse is selected. If the OEAO alternate warehouse flag is set to yes, the operator may select an alternate warehouse when it is displayed with substitutes and upgrades when the ordering warehouse is short stock. Selection of the secondary warehouse allows stock to be reserved in the alternate warehouse and transferred (a WT is generated in OEEPI) to the selling warehouse. All pricing/costing is per the selling warehouse. The alternate warehouse just provides the capability to do an automatic transfer. Content: |
| `arpprodline` | ARP Line | Character | x(6) | The ARP prodline is used for a non-stock or special order component that is sourced from a Vendor. If a prodline is entered, a valid vendor must also be entered. Content: |

| `cataddfl` | Added From Catalog | Logical | yes/no | Indicates if an order as needed product was added from the catalog when this line was added. If the product was not set up when the line was added but was defined in the catalog file, the operator has the option to create an ICSP/W record automatically. If the new records are created, this flag is set to yes. If the catalog product is pulled into the order as a non-stock product, this flag remains no. OERE reports all components added from the catalog file as lines are added. Content: |

| `cfgcompmodfl` | Cfg Comp Modified | Logical | yes/no | Configurator Integration - Component Was Modified By Configurator |

If so, when GO is pressed on the line item, oeelk.prevconv will be used to back out any ICSW quantities previously updated. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item. Content: |
| `prevprod` | Prev Product | Character | x(24) | The previous product for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.shipprod is loaded into oeelk.prevprod. When the component is updated, the oeelk.shipprod may be changed. If so, when GO is pressed on the line item, oeelk.prevprod will be used to back out any ICSW quantities previously updated. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item. Content: |
| `prevqtyord` | Prev Qty Ord | Decimal | >>>>>>9.99- | The previous quantity ordered for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.qtyord is loaded into oeelk.prevqtyord. When the component is updated, the oeelk.qtyord may be changed. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item. |
| `prevqtyrsv` | Prev Qty Rsvd | Decimal | >>>>>>>>9.99 | The previous quantity reserved is loaded from oeelk.qtyreservd prior to the change to the OE line item. It is used to properly back out the quantity reserved/committed/back ordered when changing the line from entry, during BO fill, during the commit, etc. Content: |
| `prevqtyship` | Prev Qty | Decimal | >>>>>>9.99- | The previous quantity shipped for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.qtyship is loaded into oeelk.prevqtyship. When the component is updated, the oeelk.qtyship may be changed. If so, when GO is pressed on the line item, oeelk.prevqtyship will be used to back out any ICSW quantities previously updated. This field should be zero except during change mode of the line item. |
| `prevspecns` | Prev Spec/NS | Character | x(1) | The previous special/non-stock type is used in change mode on a line item (during entry, BO fill, commit...). It is used to store the oeelk.specnstype prior to allowing change to the line or component. It is necessary to store the old value in order to properly update ICSW (back out then re-add). Content: |
| `prevunit` | Prev Unit | Character | x(4) | The previous unit for the component while in change mode. When the line item is accessed in change mode, oeelk.unit is loaded into oeelk.prevunit. When the component is updated, the oeelk.unit may be changed. This field should be blank except during change mode of the line item. |

All component records that have not been processed in KPEA will be read upon F10 update. If the machine goes down during the update, only those components not yet processed will be read for processing when the procedure is reactivated. It is set to yes once all processing is performed on a component through KPEA. Content: |

If the product is not specially costed, this field is represented in the selling unit on the component. On a stocked product, the prodcost defaults from the ICSW average, standard, replacement, or last cost plus addons (depending on what is appropriate as defined in ICAO). p-oeetlc.i is the include that sets the cost. |

### Table PDSV — PD Vendor Product Pricing

- Source page: `pdsvtbl.htm`
- Indexes: `k-pdsv` (Primary Unique), `k-prod`, `k-rowpointer` (Unique), `k-transdttmz`

| Column | Label | Type | Format | Help / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `buytype` | Qty Brk On | Character | x(1) | (Q)uantity, (W)eight, or (C)ubes |
| `cono` | Company # | Integer | >>>9 | Identifies the Company under which the record was created. |
| `enddt` | End Date | Date | 99/99/99 | The ending date for the application of this record. Not every record needs an ending date. If a PDSV record has no ending date it is considered to be in effect until another PDSV record with a later beginning date is created. A PDSV record with an ending date is used only through that date. The record will not be used after that date, regardless of whether another record exists. |
| `operinit` | Last Change By | Character | x(4) | Tags the record with the login initials of the last operator to update the record. Last update is defined by the operator pressing GO on a setup screen, or by the completion of a transaction in a batch updating process. |
| `prcdisc` | Discount | Decimal[9] | zz9.999 | If "Prices" And "Discounts" Exist, "Discounts" Will be Cleared |
| `prcmult` | Price | Decimal[9] | zzzzzz9.99999 | Price. This field provides a price for the PO. Note that this is an array of 9, each element representing another quantity break. If no quantity breaks are entered the first element will be used. Otherwise, the first level will be used until the first quantity break is met, then the program will proceed to the second level. Note that all prices are considered to be in stocking or costing unit (special pricing/costing) and that all prices are in the currency for the vendor from which the products are purchased. Note also that this is a hard dollar cost, not a multiplier or a percentage. If no quantity breaks are needed or quantity breaks are to be applied against discount levels, the 'vendorprice' field should be used and this field (ALL ELEMENTS) must be set to '0'. |

It is possible to define records with future and past start dates. Future dated records will not become effective until the start date. | `dwheight` | Height | Decimal | zzzz9.99 | This field is enterable on the PMEP Box Dimension screen if: 1. The PMEP Ship Via is UPSS - UPS Second Day Air or UPSN - UPS Next Day Air. This is new to Trend in 5.1.000f per the new UPS (feb. 7, 1994) upgrade. It is entered by the operator and used to calculate Dimensional Weight. DW = (Height x Width x Length) / 194. Dimesional Weight will override the actual weight if the cubic inches are greater than on cubic foot (H x W x L &gt;= 1728 inches) and the dimensional weight is greater than the actual weight. Dimensional Weight (H, W, L) are required on all Second Day and Next Day Air shipments in PM. Content: |
| `dwlength` | Length | Decimal | zzzz9.99 | Please reference the pmep.dwheight field for the description. |
| `dwtype` | Dimensional Type | Character | x(2) | This is the Dimensional Weight type. It was added in 5.1.000f for the new UPS Feb. 7, 1994 upgrade. It is set to 'DW' in PMEP when the dimensional weight overrides the actual PMEP weight. The conditions for dimensional weight and how it's used is defined on field dwheight (pmep). This will inform PM that this shipment is using Dimesional Weight vs. Actual Weight. PMEM will exclude dimensional weight shipments for Hundred Weight packages. Also, if the package is dimensional weigth 'DW' will display on the PMEM (Standard and Ground Saver) manifests, on the PMEP screen, when using dimesional weight, on the inquires PMILO, PMILS and the F6-Detail screen for PMILO and F8-Inquiry in PMEP. Also, drives what each weight in PMEP means: 1. If the dwtype 'DW' then pmep.origweight = actual weight and pmep.actweight = dimensional weight. 2. If the dwtype 'DW' then pmep.origweight = 0 and pmep.actweight = actual weight. |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

| `orderreppct1` | Order Rep 1 Percent | Decimal | zz9.99 | This field stores an additional order rep percentage that can be assigned to an order. Setups in ARSC will copy to ARSS on a copy and can use the AO logic to copy to ARSS if ARSC is changed (SXE-2803). When an order is created, OEEH defaults from ARSC/ARSS and then OEEL defaults from OEEH. The operator can update the assignments in OEEH/OEEL for individual order/line specifics. Once the data is stored in the OEEH/OEEL records in the database, it will be sent to DataLake and any analysis/calculations (usually for commissions) against these fields will be done in Birst. There are five of these fields that can be used. Note that the field number must match to the ordrep field number, i.e., if ordrep2 is assigned a value and you want a percentage related to that, the percentage must be specified in orderreppct2, the 2 must match on both fields to correlate them. Added with JIRA SXE-3048/SXWEB-38216. Content: |

| `geocd` | Geo Code | Integer | 999999999 | Taxware Sales and Use Tax (SUT) uses the geo code to determine which taxes should be applied if there is more than one taxing jurisdiction within a zip code. Examples of this are when a zip code crosses county lines and each county has a different tax rate or when multiple cities exist in the same zip code and each city has a different tax rate. Each taxing jurisdiction within the zip code is given a unique, two-digit identifier. Taxware uses the city name, state, zip code and geo code to find the correct tax rates. Taxware Enterprise (TWE) uses the geo code as a unique identifier of a taxing jurisdiction and not a supplemental identifier as in SUT. With TWE, all jusrisdictions world-wide have a geo code. Each geo code can include country, state or province, county, city and district taxing jurisdictions. Any taxing jurisdiction except country can be omitted from the definition of a geo code. TWE can apply the correct tax rates based on the geo code alone. Content: |

When entry or maintenance is performed on an order, the openinit is loaded with the current operator. When the operator closes the order, the openinit is cleared. This prevents 2 operators from working on the same order at the same time. We employ soft locking since we are not in a transaction state the entire time an order is entered due to potential lock table overflow problems and length of record lock problems. Content: |

A completion activity will move that portion of the totals from the "pending" fields to the "WIP" fields which reflects General Ledger updating that has occured in the WIP GL Accounts. The total value of the finished product always reflects the totals of both the pending amounts and the WIP amounts. Content: |

See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content: |
| `pndintrnest` | Pending Internal Estimated | Decimal | zzzzzzzz9.99- | This is the accumulation of all the internal processes line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP) that are also classified as "estimated" (versus actual). The estimated amount will be used as the total of the value add transaction up until the time that the actual amounts are entered. Once the actual amounts are entered, then they will be used in the calculation of the total of the finished product for the value add transaction. See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" Content: |
| `pndinvamt` | Pending Inventory Amount | Decimal | zzzzzzzz9.99- | This is the accumulation of all the inventory component sections' line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). See the pndaddons field for aa description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content: |
| `pndinvinamt` | Pending Inventory In | Decimal | zzzzzzzz9.99- | This is the accumulation of all the inventory in sections' line items that are considered in a pending status, versus Work In Process (WIP). The inventory in sections are surplus inventory that is to be returned to stock, which is a reduction (credit) of the total of the finished product for the value add transaction. This amount will always be a negative number. See the pndaddons field for a description of "pending" versus "WIP". Content: |
| `prevvano` | Previous VA Order# | Integer | zzzzzz9 | This is a user defined field on the value add transaction header screen that can be used to record the previous value add transaction# for this finished product. | `prodcost` | Cost | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99999 | The product cost of the finished product. If the finished product is specially costed, this field is represented in the special costing units. If the product is not speially costed, this field is represented in the selling unit from the value add transaction banner. The product cost is calculated by taking the total of all pending amounts (using either the actual or estimated pending internal amount) plus all the Work In Process (WIP) amounts, and dividing by the qty ordered. Content: |
| `proddesc` | Description | Character | x(24) | The product description of the finished product if it's a non-stock product. This field is enterable on the non-stock screen for a non-stock product. The description for a stocked product is not stored on the value add transaction since it is available in ICSP. |

| `qtyord` | Ordered | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | The quantity of the finished product to be fabricated on the value add transaction. This field is represented in the banner unit of measure. Content: |
| `qtyship` | Qty Ship | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | The quantity that will be fabricated for the value add transaction. It is always set to be the same as the quantity ordered, up until the time the finished product is received. At that time, the actual qty that was fabricated will be obtained from the user and placed in the qtyship. This is needed to determine if a value add transaction backorder should be created. If a value add transaction backorder is created, then the original suffix will contain the qty ordered and the actual qty shipped (different than qty ordered) and a new suffix will be created contain the difference between the 2 qtys from the original suffix and stored in both the qty ordered and qty shipped of the new suffix. The qty shipped is represented in the banner unit of measure. Content: |

It is calculated as follows: If the quantity based on total flag = yes, then it's the quantity needed * quantity ordered (vaeh.stkqtyord) of the finished product If the quantity based on total flag = no, then it's simply the quantity needed. The quantity ordered is related to the line item unit of measure. Content: |
| `qtyship` | Qty Ship | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | This is the total quantity shipped for this line item. For a stocked product, it is based on the ICSW availability. For a non-stock product, it is the quantity that has been acquired from a vendor or another warehouse and has been filled for this line item. The quantity shipped is related to the line item's unit of measure. Content: |
| `qtyunavail` |  | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | On an Inventory In section line item, the quantity returned that should not go into On Hand but that should be into unavailable (if goods are damaged, etc). This field is represented in stocking units. |
| `reasunavty` | Reason Unavailable | Character | x(2) | The reason unavailable type describes why there is unavailable quantity (qtyunavail) on the Inventory In section line item. Content: |

| `rushfl` | Rush | Logical | yes/no | If 'Yes', Then Line Will be Processed as a Rush Order |
| `scrapfctr` | Scrap Factor | Decimal | >9.99 | VA Fabrication Assembly - Identifies the Scrap Factor for the Line |
| `sctntype` | Section Type | Character | x(2) | Value add transaction section type. Each transaction section will contain one of the allowable section types (not user defined). Content: |
| `seqno` | Seq# | Integer | zz9 | Value add transaction section sequence#. Each value add section for a given transaction is assigned a unique sequence#. The sections are listed in this sequence order. Content: |
| `shipprod` | Product | Character | x(24) | This is the primary product on the VA line. It indicates the product for that line item (stock or non-stock). Content: |
| `shpqtyoverfl` | Ship Qty Over | Logical | yes/no | This flag determines if the shipping quantity has been overridden. A ship quantity override will occur when the operator types a quantity in the shipped quantity that does not match the availability of the product. |
| `statustype` | Status | Logical | active/inactive | (A)ctive, (I)nactive |
| `stkqtyord` | Stk Qty Ord | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | This is the stocking quantity ordered for this line item. |
| `stkqtyship` | Ship Qty | Decimal | zzzzzz9.99 | This is the stocking quantity shipped for this line item, based on the unit of measure. |
| `timeactty` | Actual Type | Character | x(1) | This field is used for a line item for an Internal Process or Inspection section. It is used to indicate if the line item is considered time entered as Estimated or Actual. |
| `timecomment` | Comment | Character | x(30) | This field is used for a line item for an Internal Process or Inspection section. It is used to store a comment field that can be entered when time information is entered in VAEL (similar to our CMEJ Comment field). Content: |
| `timeelapsed` | Elapsed Time | Integer | zzzzzz9 | This field is used for a line item for an Internal process or Inspection section. This field stores the time entered as total number of seconds. The user enters hours and minutes for their estimated or actual time, but the data is stored as number of seconds. Content: |
| `timeslsrep` | Sales Rep | Character | x(4) | This field is used for a line item for an Internal process or Inspection section. This is the operator's initials for the line item representing estimated or actual time. Content: |
| `timeworkdt` | Work Date | Date | 99/99/99 | This field is used for a line item for an Internal process or Inspection section. This field contains the date when the actual time was incurred. Content: |

If there at 24 stocking units in a case, the unitconv would be = 24. If we are selling 1/6 of a stocking unit, the unitconv would be = .16667. This field is used to set the stkqtyord and stkqtyship in order to update ICSW in stocking units. Content: |

| `srcrowpointer` | Source Row Pointer | Character | x(36) | Source Row Pointer. This points the the physical record of the Markup Addon type record.
